review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset label 1.0 counts as INCLUDE; 0.5 and 0.0 count as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: The abstract describes a retrospective analysis of complications following 5,851 consecutive first-trimester abortions. It is an observational cohort study, not a randomised controlled trial. Additionally, it does not compare different surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: Explicitly described as a randomised study in which 200 women requesting early abortion (gestational age <56 days) were randomised to manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) or conventional vacuum aspiration (VA). This is an RCT comparing two different surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: This is an epidemiological study comparing mortality and morbidity trends across time periods (before and after Roe v Wade). It is not a randomised controlled trial and does not compare different surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

Although the study randomly assigned participants, the comparison is between a prostaglandin vaginal suppository and a placebo prior to vacuum aspiration. The surgical procedure (vacuum aspiration) is identical in both groups; therefore it does not compare different surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: The abstract states that 420 women were randomly assigned to dilation and curettage (D&C) or vacuum aspiration (VA) for first trimester abortion. This is an RCT that directly compares two distinct surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: Described as a randomised trial in which 84 women seeking abortion at less than 10 weeks gestation were randomised to manual or electric vacuum aspiration. This is an RCT comparing two surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: Women requesting pregnancy terminations were randomly assigned to manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) or electric vacuum aspiration (EVA). This is an RCT comparing two surgical methods for first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: The abstract describes a comparison of vacuum aspiration and dilatation and curettage in 47 women but does not mention randomisation, allocation concealment, or any RCT design features. Based on title and abstract alone, this cannot be confirmed as an RCT.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: Participants were randomly assigned, but the study compares metal versus flexible plastic cannulae for performing vacuum aspiration. This compares instruments within the same surgical method rather than comparing different surgical methods (e.g., D&C, VA, MVA).

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: Described as a randomised trial of 114 women undergoing first-trimester abortions comparing manual vacuum aspiration with electric vacuum curettage. This is an RCT comparing two surgical methods for first trimester abortion.
